Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

RiboPilot 0.1.0

Before you upgrade

  • Make your existing projects again with new_project(). Projects made before this version do not record their database version and cannot be updated.
  • From this version on, a project records its database version. After a later upgrade, run backwards_compatibility() on each project instead of making it again. See “Upgrading RiboPilot” in the Installation guide.

GenBank records

  • Before it writes anything, the Export window lists every unit the BLAST screen or the chimera check flagged that nobody marked Reviewed, and leaves them out unless you choose Export anyway. Lock asks about the same units, on both tables and in the unit window, and the Export complete window names each flagged record.
  • A gene the curation step finds truncated is written as partial.
  • [organism=] uses the name confirmed in the Taxonomy step. A record whose Taxon differs gets taxon_differs(<name>) in submission_risk.
  • A gap of 5 bp or less between a gene and its spacer is closed; a larger one gets a gap warning. Assembly gaps use “unspecified” linkage evidence. An empty source modifier in a header template gives a warning.
  • Header templates are filled by column name and never run as code, and export group names must work as folder names.
  • export_project() exports every exportable unit as one “export” bundle when there are no export groups, by the same rule as the app.
  • NMNH user switch in Export data. Adds the [specimen_voucher=] and [voucherURI=] modifiers NMNH requires on GenBank submissions, fills them per sample from your mapping file, GBIF, NCBI, or GEOME, checks the voucher codes and EZIDs (a tissue EZID is replaced with its parent specimen), and reports samples that are missing or wrong. Fix them in the report or with a CSV round trip. See vignette("Sample-Metadata").
  • Click a sample ID in the NMNH voucher report to open its metadata, then return to the report. The metadata window now has a copy button on every value and Export CSV to save all of a sample’s metadata.
  • Tick Not NMNH in the voucher report for samples that are not NMNH specimens: their voucher and URI are used as found, without NMNH checks. For any sample, pick the mapping-file column or metadata field its specimen_voucher or voucherURI comes from.
  • The NMNH user switch is remembered per project. The voucher report’s field lists are sorted and offer None to leave a modifier out.
  • A [modifier={field}] with no value for a sample is left out of that record’s FASTA header instead of being written empty.

Chimera check in the sequence viewer

  • The chimera evidence now lives in the sequence viewer of the Assemble and Annotation Review windows: a BLAST origin track colors each stretch by the class its BLAST windows match (gray is the sample’s own lineage), a BLAST identity track shows the hit identity, and dashed lines mark possible junctions. Hover for the match. The static chimera plot is gone.
  • The Windowed BLAST details panel shows the reason under the call instead of on hover, says “not run” after a trim, and lists windows under their segment. Clicking a segment, window, or junction row zooms the viewer to it. On the Assemble window, a flagged contig opens the viewer by itself.
  • The lineage palette is down to three colors that stay apart under red-green color blindness.

Quality checks

  • A Checks column on the Assemble and Annotation Review tables sums up each sample or unit: red for off target, contaminant, severe chimera, or ITSx chimeric; amber for things worth a look; green “ok”.
  • Chimera calls are clean, minor, or severe. Only severe calls are a submission risk; minor calls are listed in the report.
  • Each core feature (18S, ITS1, 5.8S, ITS2, 28S) is now searched on its own against the bundled rDNA database. A new Feature BLAST warnings column in Annotation Review lists features with no hit, a non-rDNA hit, a hit outside the sample’s phylum, or too short to search (under 50 bp), and a Feature BLAST panel in the details window shows each feature’s matches. Its Search column names the algorithm that found the hit; a hit found only by the more sensitive dc-megablast retry is shown in amber and listed as a weak hit.
  • Window searches in the chimera check keep up to 5000 hits and count one record per taxon, so a genome annotation with hundreds of identical rRNA copies no longer fills the hit list and poses as a confident match to a distant species. A window whose whole hit list is one taxon counts as unresolved. Ties now read “(N tied taxa)”.
  • The chimera check now searches 150 bp windows end to end with no overlap (was 500 bp windows every 250 bp), so it catches shorter foreign stretches and every base belongs to one window. A switch between classes still needs about 450 bp on each side, which keeps conserved stretches from raising false alarms.
  • Windows with no hit, or an unresolved one, no longer split a lineage in two: stretches of the same class on either side of them count as one side of a possible switch. A chimera whose foreign part sits next to a poorly matched stretch of the host is no longer missed.
  • Changing a sample’s taxon updates its lineage and screens it again. A name that matches more than one organism is never picked automatically.
  • Isomer and paralog classes are computed after annotation finishes.

Annotation Review edits and Update

  • Trims, gene boundary edits, and 5’/3’ choices on Annotation Review change a working copy of the contig. The original contig and its check results stay as the pipeline made them, and the Assemble step shows only the original.
  • A trim or a boundary edit marks the contig’s checks “not run”. The new Update button on Annotation Review reruns every offline check on those contigs, one contig at a time: feature counts, gene completeness, ITSx, the BLAST hits, the BLAST screen, the reference alignment, the quality flags, and the chimera check. It never re-annotates and never contacts NCBI. Quality flags are no longer recalculated in the app right after an edit.
  • State on Annotation Review offers only Ready to run and On hold, and queues contigs for that Update. A contig whose original still waits for the Assemble step’s Update says so.
  • Lock on Annotation Review refuses the whole click when a selected contig’s checks are not finished, and lists those contigs with what to do next. Exclude & Lock still works. Export leaves such contigs out and counts them.
  • Restore deletes the working copy, so the contig shows its original sequence, features, and checks again. It undoes trims, boundary edits, and 5’/3’ choices; marks, notes, and export group stay. Restore on the toolbar works on any contig with a working copy, not only trimmed ones.
  • Export no longer runs ITSx. The itsx_check column of <group>_summary.csv and the Export done window report the ITSx check stored for each contig, and <group>_itsx_check.csv and the itsx_check/ folder are gone. An ITSx run that crashed reads not_run(ITSx did not finish), never clean, and the Checks column shows it as “ITSx not checked”.
  • Existing projects need backwards_compatibility() once. It turns earlier trims and edits into working copies and puts the original contigs back.

Re-running samples

  • Assembling a sample again clears the old genes, screen, chimera call, BLAST results, lock, and marks of every contig whose sequence changed. Your own keep and drop calls follow their sequence.
  • Changing annotation options re-runs only annotation. A contig you trimmed or edited on Annotation Review keeps its edits, and its checks are queued for Update on Annotation Review; Restore takes the new annotation.
  • Annotation options take extra command-line flags for the rRNA caller, one field for pybarrnap and one for barrnap, since the two take different flags. The flags go to both per-contig annotation and the rRNA scan of a supplied assembly. Existing projects need backwards_compatibility() once.
  • Changing a BLAST setting searches again.
  • A rescue with the baited assembler is annotated in the same run.
  • An rRNA scan of a supplied assembly that does not finish fails the sample instead of keeping part of the result.

Runs

  • The end of a run says “Run finished with no failures”, or names each failed sample and step with the exit code and the likely cause. Copy report copies the report.
  • Run Reports in the toolbar lists every run, reference build, and cluster job, with its result, and shows each one’s report. The app says when a run it did not watch, such as a cluster job, has finished. While open, the window checks every 15 seconds for new runs and for runs that have finished. The run list fits its runs and scrolls past 10.
  • Run files go in the project’s .runs/ folder: job scripts, scheduler logs, Nextflow logs, and reports. Runs from run_assembly() get their own log there too.
  • A failed sample’s window says why it failed and what to try next.
  • Closing the browser tab, or pressing Stop or Stop and Close in the run window, stops a run cleanly. Only one run goes at a time per project.
  • Each task is capped at this computer’s CPUs and memory.
  • The rescue for a failed sample is the baited SPAdes choice under Assembler in Assembly Options; run_fallback() is removed.
  • Cluster job scripts for SLURM, SGE, PBS, and LSF take the queue, account, and walltime from your profile. The awsbatch profile is removed.

Projects

  • new_project() and new_test_project() work outside RStudio and use Docker by default. Conda is unsupported and warns.
  • The mapping file, IDs, and paths are checked before anything is written.
  • New add_samples() and update_sample_metadata().
  • New backwards_compatibility() updates a project’s database and points the project at the container image for the installed RiboPilot, after saving a copy of both. The next run downloads that image by itself. The app does not open a project that needs this update, and says how to run it.
  • A locked unit is read only. Problematic is now Exclude from export. Lock & Close only locks; Mark Reviewed is separate. Only one assembly path per sample can be locked.
  • The Reference groups table’s record count is now “# GenBank Hits”, and a new “# Database Sequences” column shows how many sequences a built database holds. The build drops duplicate and short records, so it is usually much smaller.
  • After you change the reference folder, Propose groups points each group at that folder’s database, or marks it as needing one. Databases you picked yourself from elsewhere are kept.

Working at scale, reproducibility, and clusters

  • The Assemble details window has a Notes box for your own notes on a sample. They show in the Assemble table’s User notes column, and a unit’s notes show in the Annotation Review table’s User notes column.
  • The Partial column reads “no” for every unit not marked Partial, so a filter on “no” lists only complete units.
  • The Checks column can be dragged wider.
  • The chimera check panel follows the contig’s edits: after a trim or a feature boundary edit it says “Not run yet. Press Update.” until the recheck has run, and after a Restore it shows the original check again. A contig waiting for the Assemble step’s Update shows “Waiting for the Assemble step’s Update.” there.
  • Trim and Restore buttons on the Assemble and Annotation Review toolbars trim many units at once, to their gene ends or gene ends plus a flank, and undo it. Only units with all five features are trimmed; the window lists the rest and why before you confirm.
  • The Lock and State filters now drop rows from the underlying table instead of hiding them with CSS, so the table’s paging and counts always match what the filters allow; refreshing the table keeps its page and selection. The header tick box, bulk actions, and Triage all act only on rows the search and column filters still show, and Triage skips assembly-locked samples with a toast rather than silently including them.
  • Clicking a row’s lock or state icon on the Taxonomy, Assemble, and Annotation Review tables locks, unlocks, or sets the state of that row alone, with the same questions as the toolbar buttons. The Unlock and “Edit beyond the selection” questions have a “Don’t ask again this session” box.
  • Every tool chain package in the container image is pinned to the version actually installed, and the pins match environment.yml.
  • Opening a project whose container image is for another RiboPilot version shows a message that says so and how to switch; runs carry on with that image.
  • The database that answered a unit’s BLAST search (the bundled rDNA database, with its version, or NCBI core_nt) is recorded for every unit, and the BLAST evidence panel names it.
  • On the NMNH Hydra cluster, the rRNA search of a supplied assembly, and the other per-sample memory steps, ask Hydra for memory the way it expects.

Sample metadata

  • new_test_project() now fetches each sample’s NCBI metadata from its SRA run (CHIM00 and CHIM01 use the Upeneus parvus run they were built from) and follows links to GBIF and GEOME, with linking saved as the project setting. Pass fetch_metadata = FALSE when offline.
  • Link samples to GEOME, GBIF, and NCBI BioSample records through mapping-file columns GEOME_BCID, GBIF_ID, and BioSample, or other names via mapping_geome, mapping_gbif, and mapping_ncbi.
  • new_project(), new_test_project(), add_samples(), and update_sample_metadata() fetch the records, unless fetch_geome, fetch_gbif, or fetch_ncbi is FALSE. link_sources = TRUE also follows links between databases.
  • New fetch_geome(), fetch_gbif(), fetch_ncbi(), remove_metadata(), and set_metadata_columns(), plus geome_normalize_bcid(), gbif_normalize_id(), and ncbi_normalize_id().
  • The NCBI API key is read from the project .config, then NCBI_API_KEY, then ENTREZ_KEY.
  • A Metadata column in the Taxonomy, Assemble, Annotation Review, and Export tables opens a viewer with per-source tabs and a Compare tab.
  • One Metadata fields window, opened by the Metadata button, picks both which metadata fields show as table columns (Show) and which can be used at export (Export). Tick both together sets both with one click, header boxes tick every row in view, GenBank-ready and Ticked only narrow the list, sample counts show gaps (for example 12/20), and a click copies a field’s template text. Choose fields in Export Data opens the same window filtered to that source. Export fields go into header templates and <group>_summary.csv. Export asks before writing when sources disagree on something a template uses. A mapping-file column with the same name as a ticked field wins.
  • Linking to GBIF by voucher follows Darwin Core. When a GEOME or NCBI record has no Smithsonian EZID, RiboPilot searches GBIF for the specimen voucher in every field that can hold one (specimen_voucher, genbankSpecimenVoucher, materialSampleID, voucherCatalogNumber, otherCatalogNumbers, bio_material, or a bare catalog number with the institution code). It reads triplets, doublets, urn:catalog: prefixes, and USNM 419933-style spacing, keeps the only match even when its collection code differs, and skips GBIF occurrences copied from GenBank or BOLD.
  • geome_specimen_voucher uses genbankSpecimenVoucher when GEOME has it, and gbif_specimen_voucher drops a catalog number’s leading repeat of the institution code.

Documentation

  • A new Get started guide that follows the app: a short page on setup, then a test project walkthrough with one page per step (Taxonomy, Reference, Assemble, Annotation Review, Export). Boxes tagged HYDRA mark where the NMNH Hydra cluster differs.
  • New pages on installation, your own project, GenBank submission, scripting, clusters, caches and offline use, troubleshooting, and citing RiboPilot.
  • This changelog, citation("RiboPilot"), and the tool versions in the container image, for methods sections.
  • The docs and the app say “contig” where they said “scaffold”: every assembled sequence is gapless. Names you type or read in files are unchanged: the scaffold column and {scaffold} header token, max_scaffolds, and record names such as SRR33849683_p1_s2.
  • The bundled example is called the test project, as in MitoPilot.
  • The docs and the app use the same names: “step”, “BLAST screen”, and “bundled rDNA database”. RiboPilot does not ship a reference database; build one for every group in the Reference step.
  • Help pages show their formatting and links.
